clue.text: Cameron, gathering backbench support, has a brief moment of calm

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other
something brief is cut short, so the phrase loses its last letter

blocks.note: David Cameron was Prime Minister, abbreviated PM
the back of bench is its last letter
a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: David Cameron, propped up by his backbenchers, enjoys a short spell of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbench' suggests MPs on the rear benches, but it means the back of the word bench. 'Moment of calm' looks like one phrase; 'of' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic person is unexcitable and composed, a synonym for calm in temperament.

clue.text: Prepared canapé wrapping gutted trout in bacon

blocks.note: the letters of canapé rearranged
the first and last letters of trout

explanation.surface: A recipe: a canapé made by wrapping cleaned trout in bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like part of the recipe, but it is the definition, with 'in' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is Italian cured pork belly, a type of bacon.

clue.text: Remained decorous in speech

explanation.surface: Someone kept polite in the way they talked.
explanation.walkthrough: Staid and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in place, a simple past-tense synonym.

explanation.definitionFit: A yurt is a round felt tent used by nomads in Central Asia.

clue.text: Twisted rambling vine round new helter-skelter tower

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A twisting vine climbs around a new fairground helter-skelter tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helter-skelter' looks like a fairground slide but works as a second anagram signal; all the letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Interwoven strands are twisted together, so the adjective matches twisted.

clue.text: Lobby for Conservative politician to capture a potential gain

a Member of Parliament
taken as written
the letters of gain rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to confuse or puzzle them, a synonym of bewilder.

clue.text: Joint for Ken and Barbie finally cooked

the last letter of Barbie

the letters of run rearranged

clue.text: A number, I included, dined at home

blocks.note: taken as written
ten is a number
taken as written

clue.text: Scramble record containing name and call time

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

clue.text: Support earth on steep banks leading to great river

the first and last letters of steep

the first letter of Telegraph

clue.text: Sailor returns to ship after day involved in alcohol and ribaldry

explanation.walkthrough: An able seaman is abbreviated AB, a standard crossword sailor; the steamship prefix supplies the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawdiness is coarse, sexual humour, the same thing as ribaldry.

clue.text: Older sibling keeping an eye on us?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a brother older than you and the surveillance state figure from Orwell's novel.

taken as written

taken as written

drunk means tipsy

explanation.definitionFit: To cut and run is the idiom for leaving hurriedly, making a quick escape.

clue.text: Makes fun of Great Aunt Sally's stuffing

blocks.note: found running through these words

the second letter of hand
